hints.text: An exponent tells you how many times the base is used as a factor. How many tens get multiplied here?
The exponent is $3$, so write three tens and multiply them: $10 \times 10 \times 10$. Start with $10 \times 10 = 100$.
$100 \times 10 = 1000$, so $10^3$ equals $1000$, a one followed by three zeros.

explanation: The exponent $3$ means the base $10$ is used as a factor three times: $10^3 = 10 \times 10 \times 10$.
Multiply two of the tens first to get $10 \times 10 = 100$.
Multiply by the last ten: $100 \times 10 = 1000$, so $10^3 = 1000$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Zero-counting shortcut
steps: A power of ten has as many zeros as its exponent.
